ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *kewp-der. Latin cūpa ▲ Frankish *koppinflu.? Late Latin cuppabor.? Proto-Indo-European *gew-der. Proto-Germanic *kuppaz? Old English cuppe ▲ Proto-Germanic *kuppaz Old English copp Middle English cuppe, coppe English cup Inherited from Middle English cuppe, coppe, from the merger of Old English cuppe (“cup”) and Old English copp (“cup, vessel”). Old English cuppe is a borrowing from Late Latin cuppa, itself of obscure origin, but probably from earlier Latin cūpa (“tub, cask”), from Proto-Indo-European *kewp- (“a hollow”).

senses.d: A concave vessel for drinking, usually made of opaque material (as opposed to a glass) and with a handle.
ex: Pour the tea into the cup.
I drank two cups of water but still felt thirsty.
In Starbucks’s case, the firm has in effect turned the process of making an expensive cup of coffee into intellectual property.

senses.d: A US unit of liquid measure equal to 8 fluid ounces (¹⁄₁₆ of a US gallon; 236.5882365 mL) or 240 mL.
A Canadian unit of measure equal to 8 imperial ounces (¹⁄₂₀ imperial gallon; 227.3 mL) or 250 mL.
A British unit of measure equal to ¹⁄₂ imperial pint (10 imperial ounces; 284 mL) or 300 mL.
A metric unit of measure equal to 250 mL.
A trophy in the shape of an oversized cup.
ex: The World Cup is awarded to the winner of a quadrennial football tournament.

senses.d: A contest for which a cup is awarded.
ex: The World Cup is the world's most widely watched sporting event.

senses.d: The main knockout tournament in a country, organised alongside the league.
ex: Until it was disbanded in 1999, the European Cup-Winners Cup was contested annually by the winners of Europe's national cups.
Wallace had the unique distinction of being the only player ever to play in the English, Welsh and Scottish Cups in the same season.

senses.d: A cup-shaped object placed in the target hole.
ex: The ball just misses the cup.

senses.d: To form into the shape of a cup, particularly of the hands.
ex: Cup your hands and I'll pour some rice into them.

senses.d: To hold something in cupped hands.
ex: He cupped the ball carefully in his hands.

senses.d: To pour (a liquid, drink, etc.) into a cup.
ex: We are cupping some new brands of coffee today.

senses.d: To supply with cups of wine.
ex: Cup us, till the world go round.

senses.d: To apply a cup or cupping apparatus to; to subject to the operation of cupping.
To make concave or in the form of a cup.
ex: to cup the end of a screw
